quests.definition: Genuine, real, and true to original traditions rather than an imitation.
quests.example: The chef insisted on using only authentic Italian ingredients for the pasta.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: The chef insisted on using only authentic Italian ingredients for the pasta.
quests.nativeTip: Native speakers often describe honest, grounded people as 'very authentic'.
quests.commonMistake: Don't confuse 'authentic' with 'original' — an original idea is new; an authentic item is real and genuine.

teachingCards.title: AUTHENTIC — Core Meaning & Usage
teachingCards.explanation:
Genuine, real, and true to original traditions rather than an imitation.

Example: "The chef insisted on using only authentic Italian ingredients for the pasta."
teachingCards.nativeSpeakerInsight: Native speakers often describe honest, grounded people as 'very authentic'.

quests.definition: Able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions or setbacks.
quests.example: The startup proved resilient after losing its main investor in the first quarter.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: The startup proved resilient after losing its main investor in the first quarter.
quests.nativeTip: 'Resilient' is widely used in performance reviews to praise mental toughness.
quests.commonMistake: Don't confuse 'resilient' with 'resistant' — resistant blocks things; resilient recovers when knocked down.

teachingCards.title: RESILIENT — Core Meaning & Usage
teachingCards.explanation:

Example: "The startup proved resilient after losing its main investor in the first quarter."
teachingCards.nativeSpeakerInsight: 'Resilient' is widely used in performance reviews to praise mental toughness.

quests.definition: Featuring new methods, advanced ideas, or creative originality.
quests.example: The engineering team designed an innovative solar battery for rural clinics.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: The engineering team designed an innovative solar battery for rural clinics.
quests.nativeTip: Pronounce it with stress on the first syllable 'IN-no-va-tive'.
quests.commonMistake: Don't say 'an innovative' without a following noun — use 'an innovative idea' or 'an innovation'.

teachingCards.title: INNOVATIVE — Core Meaning & Usage
teachingCards.explanation:
Featuring new methods, advanced ideas, or creative originality.

Example: "The engineering team designed an innovative solar battery for rural clinics."
teachingCards.nativeSpeakerInsight: Pronounce it with stress on the first syllable 'IN-no-va-tive'.

quests.definition: To work jointly with others on an activity or project to produce something.
quests.example: Two rival research universities agreed to collaborate on cancer immunotherapy.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: Two rival research universities agreed to collaborate on cancer immunotherapy.
quests.nativeTip: Always use the preposition 'with' for people/teams and 'on' for projects.

quests.definition: A particular attitude toward or way of regarding something; a point of view.
quests.example: Traveling alone gave her a fresh perspective on international cultural differences.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: Traveling alone gave her a fresh perspective on international cultural differences.
quests.nativeTip: Say 'from my perspective' instead of 'in my opinion' to sound more professional in meetings.

quests.definition: Sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention; noteworthy.
quests.example: The clinical study reported a significant decrease in patient recovery times.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: The clinical study reported a significant decrease in patient recovery times.
quests.nativeTip: In statistical and research contexts, 'statistically significant' has a strict mathematical meaning.
quests.commonMistake: Don't say 'more significant' when something is binary — use 'much more significant impact'.

quests.definition: To increase speed, cause to happen sooner, or progress more rapidly.
quests.example: The government invested heavily to accelerate the transition to clean electric vehicles.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: The government invested heavily to accelerate the transition to clean electric vehicles.
quests.nativeTip: Often paired with non-physical nouns like 'progress', 'timeline', or 'growth'.
quests.commonMistake: Don't say 'accelerate faster' — 'accelerate' already includes the concept of going faster.

quests.definition: Complete, thorough, and including or dealing with all elements or aspects.
quests.example: The new hire underwent a comprehensive safety training program before starting.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: The new hire underwent a comprehensive safety training program before starting.
quests.commonMistake: A report that is 'comprehensive' is complete; a report that is 'comprehensible' is readable.

teachingCards.title: COMPREHENSIVE — Core Meaning & Usage

quests.definition: Having made a firm decision and being resolved not to change it; resolute.
quests.example: Despite the stormy weather, the rescue team was determined to reach the stranded hikers.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: Despite the stormy weather, the rescue team was determined to reach the stranded hikers.
quests.nativeTip: Follow with 'to + verb' (e.g. 'determined to win') or use before a noun ('determined effort').
quests.commonMistake: Pronounce it with two syllables in the suffix: 'de-TER-mind', not 'de-ter-mi-ned'.

teachingCards.title: DETERMINED — Core Meaning & Usage
teachingCards.explanation:

teachingCards.nativeSpeakerInsight: Follow with 'to + verb' (e.g. 'determined to win') or use before a noun ('determined effort').

quests.definition: The ability to accomplish a job with minimum expenditure of time, effort, and cost.
quests.example: Upgrading the factory conveyor belts increased overall production efficiency by 20%.
quests.realWorldContextSentence: Upgrading the factory conveyor belts increased overall production efficiency by 20%.
quests.nativeTip: 'Efficiency' is doing things right with minimal waste; 'effectiveness' is doing the right things.
quests.commonMistake: Don't confuse 'efficiency' (speed/resource usage) with 'efficacy' (ability to cure/work).

teachingCards.title: EFFICIENCY — Core Meaning & Usage
teachingCards.explanation:

teachingCards.nativeSpeakerInsight: 'Efficiency' is doing things right with minimal waste; 'effectiveness' is doing the right things.
